answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, time-vested stake before it may transact, like a narrow inlet that only admits one boat at a time. New agents enter through a slow, public meadow of reputation: peers attest real work over days, and stake slashing punishes fake identities. Like a river that gathers many small streams into one verifiable flow, the ledger merges attestations into a single trust score, so creating thousands of cheap copies costs more than any single copy can earn.
